title: A power series: radius, interval, a derivative and a geometric sum

stimulus.title: The power series for $f$
stimulus.text: The function $f$ is defined by the power series $f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 5^n}$ for all $x$ where the series converges. Its first three terms are shown.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the ratio test to find the radius of convergence of the series for $f$.

rubric.point: Sets up the ratio with absolute values and finds its limit: $\lim_{n \to \infty} \left|\frac{(x - 2)^{n+1}}{(n + 1)5^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 5^n}{(x - 2)^n}\right| = \frac{|x - 2|}{5}$
accept: the limit written with $n \to \infty$ and absolute value bars

parts.sample: $\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right| = \frac{|x - 2|^{n+1}}{(n + 1)5^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 5^n}{|x - 2|^n} = \frac{|x - 2|}{5} \cdot \frac{n}{n + 1}$, so $\lim_{n \to \infty} \left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right| = \frac{|x - 2|}{5}$. The series converges when $\frac{|x - 2|}{5} < 1$, that is $|x - 2| < 5$. The radius of convergence is 5.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the interval of convergence of the series for $f$. Justify your answer at each endpoint.

rubric.point: Right endpoint: at $x = 7$ the series is $\sum \frac{1}{n}$, the harmonic series, which diverges
Left endpoint: at $x = -3$ the series is $\sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$, which converges by the alternating series test, with the conditions stated (alternates; $\frac{1}{n}$ decreases and approaches 0)
accept: "alternating harmonic series, which converges" with the conditions of the alternating series test

rubric.point: Interval $[-3, 7)$, consistent with the endpoint conclusions

parts.sample: From part (a), the series converges for $-3 < x < 7$. At $x = 7$: $\sum \frac{5^n}{n \cdot 5^n} = \sum \frac{1}{n}$, the harmonic series, which diverges. At $x = -3$: $\sum \frac{(-5)^n}{n \cdot 5^n} = \sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$; the terms alternate in sign, and $\frac{1}{n}$ decreases and approaches 0, so this series converges by the alternating series test. The interval of convergence is $[-3, 7)$.

parts.label: c
parts.sample: The series is the Taylor series for $f$ about $x = 2$, so the coefficient of $(x - 2)^3$ is $\frac{f'''(2)}{3!}$. That coefficient is $\frac{1}{3 \cdot 125} = \frac{1}{375}$, so $f'''(2) = 3! \cdot \frac{1}{375} = \frac{6}{375} = \frac{2}{125}$.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write the power series for $f'(x)$, using sigma notation. Then use it to find the exact value of $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{2^{n-1}}{5^n}$.

rubric.point: Recognizes the sum as $f'(4)$, a geometric series with first term $\frac{1}{5}$ and ratio $\frac{2}{5}$, and finds $\frac{1/5}{1 - 2/5} = \frac{1}{3}$

parts.sample: Differentiating term by term, $\frac{d}{dx}\frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 5^n} = \frac{n(x - 2)^{n-1}}{n \cdot 5^n}$, so $f'(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 2)^{n-1}}{5^n}$ for $|x - 2| < 5$. At $x = 4$ this is $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{2^{n-1}}{5^n}$, a geometric series with first term $\frac{1}{5}$ and ratio $\frac{2}{5}$. Its sum is $\frac{1/5}{1 - 2/5} = \frac{1/5}{3/5} = \frac{1}{3}$.
